curvatrip.title: CurvaTrip
summary: CurvaTrip is the conversational AI behind the chat and voice screens of the CurvaTrip flight-booking app. A visitor can type or speak a request in plain language — “cheapest flight to Paris next weekend for two” — and the agent searches a live GDS, filters by learned preferences, prices the fare, and walks the user to payment.

The agent exposes 32 tools over flights, bookings, trip planning and notifications. Language handling is a first-class concern: an LLM classifier picks the reply language between English, French, Arabic and Tunisian Derja, with Derja written from a real phrasebook rather than machine-translated Modern Standard Arabic.
Voice runs through a Gemini Live bridge with barge-in, so a caller can interrupt mid-sentence. Voice replies carry the same flight cards and trip plans as the chat and persist to the same history.
highlights: 32 agent tools: flight search and refinement, fare rules, branded fares, cheapest-dates, booking, cancellation, price alerts, trip planning, weather, currency and support
Booking is gated behind payment — the API emits a checkout event so the app opens the SATIM gateway, and a booking that cannot be ticketed degrades to a held PNR instead of failing outright
Day-by-day trip plans with photos, price bands, distances and tips, built from disk-cached catalogs to keep plan generation responsive
Realtime voice over a Gemini Live bridge (PCM16, 16 kHz in / 24 kHz out) with barge-in support
SQLite for development, Oracle 11g in production, bridged by a hand-written dialect-translating data layer
17 golden behaviour scenarios run as an eval harness — language choice, payment gating, guest isolation, round-trip legs, multi-city and more

notes.title: Sticky routing was not optional
notes.body: Flight catalogs live in RAM between turns, so a request that lands on a different instance loses the user's context. nginx hashes on user id plus remote address to keep a session pinned. An early config capped failover retries at 3 while running 16 instances — users hashed to a stopped port failed until the retry count matched the pool size.

notes.title: Derja is a dialect, not a translation
notes.body: Machine-translating Modern Standard Arabic produces text Tunisians do not speak. The reply language is chosen by an LLM classifier and Derja responses are written from a dedicated phrasebook, in both chat and voice.

notes.title: Built on an open-source runtime
notes.body: The agent loop, tool registry and memory come from Hermes Agent (NousResearch, MIT). The travel product — tools, planner, language stack, voice bridge, server and app — is my own code on top of it.

hotel-contract-saas.title: Hotel Contract SaaS
summary: Hotel contracts arrive as PDFs, Word files and spreadsheets, each laid out differently, and every rate in them has to be read by hand before a stay can be quoted. This platform reads them automatically: an LLM extraction pipeline with an OCR fallback turns a contract into a normalized Oracle schema of 17 tables — seasons, rooms, rates, supplements, reductions, taxes, offers, cancellation and payment rules.

Pricing is deliberately kept away from the model. A deterministic pure-Python engine prices any stay from the extracted tables and pre-builds a full pricing matrix per contract, so a quote is reproducible and auditable rather than something a language model guessed.

Hermes, the in-app assistant, sits on top with 12 tools. It answers questions about a contract, computes prices, finds gaps in the extracted data and proposes field edits — always behind a dry-run then confirm flow, so nothing is written to a contract without review.
highlights: Dual-path extraction pipeline (V1 + V2) with an OCR fallback for scanned contracts, driven by a 45 KB JSON schema
Deterministic pricing engine — no LLM in the pricing path — with matrix build, Excel export and a per-stay breakdown
Assistant with 12 tools: price calculation, hotel lookup, contract sections, field descriptions, gap finding, autofill suggestions, rescan and matrix rebuild
Row-level multi-tenancy: the tenant id comes from the JWT and is injected into every Oracle query, with per-tenant document cabinets
Oracle-backed async upload queue using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with a worker pool, so batch ingests do not block the API
Parse-quality scoring, missing-field detection, audit log and per-event billing for uploads and rescans
Production guards: the app refuses to boot on a default JWT secret, and API docs are disabled outside development

notes.title: Why pricing never calls the model
notes.body: A quote that cannot be reproduced cannot be sold. The LLM's job ends once the contract is structured; every price after that comes from plain Python over the extracted tables, which makes each figure traceable to a rule and a row.

notes.title: Tenant isolation by construction
notes.body: Rather than filtering in the service layer, the tenant id from the JWT is threaded into the data layer and applied to every query — around 370 call sites — so a missing filter is a compile-time-visible omission, not a silent leak.

travel-crm.title: Travel CRM & Analytics Platform
summary: An enterprise travel CRM where the reporting layer is a conversation. Instead of clicking through dashboards, a manager asks a question and an 8-agent system decides which specialist should answer it: SQL, Analyst, Forecast, Anomaly, Segmentation, Hotel, Flight, or the Orchestrator that routes between them.

The agents run on LangGraph with DeepSeek through OpenRouter, over an Oracle 11.2g database exposed by 52 FastAPI endpoints. Answers stream back over SSE so long analyses render progressively instead of blocking.
The Angular 17 dashboard renders the results as interactive charts and maps, and a separate ingestion path parses hotel contract PDFs with OCR.
highlights: 8 specialised agents coordinated by an orchestrator, each with its own tools and prompt
52 REST endpoints over Oracle 11.2g
SSE streaming so multi-step analyses appear as they are produced
Angular 17 dashboard with interactive charts and real-time route maps
Hotel contract PDF parsing with OCR
Amadeus API integration for flight and fare data

52 endpoints"] B --> C["Orchestrator agent"] C --> D["SQL agent"] C --> E["Analyst agent"] C --> F["Forecast agent"] C --> G["Anomaly agent"] C --> H["Segmentation agent"] C --> I["Hotel agent"] C --> J["Flight agent"] D --> K[("Oracle 11.2g")] I --> L["PDF + OCR parsing"] J --> M["Amadeus API"] C --> N["LangGraph + DeepSeek"]

notes.title: Routing beats one big prompt
notes.body: A single agent holding every tool degrades as the toolset grows. Splitting the work into specialists behind an orchestrator keeps each prompt small and makes a wrong answer traceable to one agent.

summary: A multi-page Streamlit application for analysing and predicting stock performance on the Bourse des Valeurs Mobilières de Tunis. Built as a Data Science engineering project at ESPRIT with the Company Value team.

Ten modules cover the market end to end: historical quotations, TUNINDEX and sector indices, dividend forecasting, risk classification, price-direction prediction, clustering, news sentiment, and a RAG chatbot that answers questions about an uploaded PDF.

Stock risk classification into low and high risk bands
Dividend forecasting with Prophet
Market clustering with DBSCAN over UMAP-reduced features
RAG chatbot: upload a PDF and ask questions, backed by LangChain, FAISS and Llama 2 through Ollama
Market sentiment from scraped Tunisian financial news
Historical data 2016–2023 stored in MongoDB Atlas, collected with Selenium and BeautifulSoup

anomaly-detection.title: Anomaly & Intrusion Detection
anomaly-detection.tagline: GMM + Decision Tree / KNN on NSL-KDD
summary: Two complementary approaches to network security on the NSL-KDD dataset. Gaussian Mixture Models learn what normal traffic looks like and flag deviations, which catches novel behaviour without labelled examples of it.
A supervised layer then classifies known intrusions with Decision Tree and K-Nearest Neighbors across four attack families: DoS, User-to-Root, Remote-to-Local and Probe.
highlights: Unsupervised anomaly detection with Gaussian Mixture Models over normal-traffic distributions
Supervised intrusion classification into DoS, U2R, R2L and Probe
Decision Tree and KNN compared on the same preprocessed feature set
Full preprocessing pipeline: cleaning, encoding and scaling of NSL-KDD

time-series-fred.title: Time Series — Federal Reserve (FRED)
summary: A three-phase study of two economic series from the Federal Reserve Economic Data archive: retail sales for book stores (MRTSSM451211USN) and new privately-owned housing units started in the Northeast (HOUSTNENSA).

Phase one argues a modelling strategy from statistical and graphical analysis — structural breaks, random walk versus polynomial trend, seasonality. Phase two fits the series through differencing and functional forms and compares candidate models. Phase three analyses the residuals to confirm the fit holds.
highlights: Stationarity testing with ADF and KPSS
Trend and seasonality decomposition, including structural-break detection
Variance-stabilising transformations before modelling
ARIMA and SARIMA candidates compared on the same series
Residual diagnostics as an explicit third phase rather than an afterthought

knowledge-graph.title: Knowledge Graph for Project Management
summary: A graph-based recommendation system for project risk management. The knowledge graph is built from PMI standards, PMBOK 6 and 7, a risk-management glossary and real case studies, so recommendations are grounded in the discipline's own literature.

Two recommenders were built and compared: one using BERT embeddings with a custom link predictor, and one combining BERT embeddings with a Relational Graph Convolutional Network for richer structural context before the same predictor.
highlights: Knowledge graph assembled from PMI standards, PMBOK 6 & 7 and case studies
BERT embeddings for semantic representation of graph entities
RGCN over the relational graph for structure-aware embeddings
Custom link-prediction head driving the recommendations
Pinecone vector index for similarity search
GPT-4 Mini for natural-language question answering over the graph

simple-api-logger.title: Simple API Logger
simple-api-logger.tagline: FastAPI request logging with a live dashboard
summary: A lightweight REST service that logs every request passing through it and renders the results on a live dashboard. Custom middleware captures the method, URL, body, status code and response time of each call, storing them in SQLite.
It includes a deliberate failure switch: posting a message of trigger500 causes a division by zero, so error handling and error logging can be exercised on demand rather than hoped about.
highlights: POST /api/log to record an entry, GET /api/logs with status and limit filters, GET /api/stats for analytics
Statistics cover total requests, 2xx versus error counts, average response time and most-hit endpoints
Custom ASGI middleware captures every request including failures
Bootstrap 5 and Jinja2 dashboard that auto-refreshes every 5 seconds
trigger500 mechanism for testing error paths on purpose

hotel-nearest-places.title: Hotel Nearest Places
summary: A Flask REST API that takes a hotel name and returns the ten nearest points of interest, each with a road distance, a route and current weather.

The interesting part is the front of the pipeline: instead of a geocoding service, an LLM extracts the hotel's coordinates and candidate nearby places from natural language, and OpenStreetMap data is used to enrich and verify what comes back.
highlights: LLM-powered geocoding with Groq running Llama 3 8B
Road distances and directions from OpenRouteService
Current conditions per point of interest from OpenWeatherMap
POI enrichment through Overpass and OpenStreetMap
CORS-enabled Flask REST API

minecraft-llm-bot.title: Minecraft LLM Bot
summary: An LLM connected to a Minecraft server over RCON. It moderates chat, answers player questions in-game, and turns operator instructions written in plain English into the right server commands.

Commands are never executed blind: the model proposes the command, the operator confirms it, and only then does it run. A raw prefix bypasses the model entirely when you already know the exact syntax.
highlights: Chat moderation: every message is analysed, with escalation from warning to kick to ban
Players ask questions with ?bot and get an in-game reply
Natural language to server command, with an explicit confirmation step before execution
!raw prefix to send a command directly, bypassing the model
RCON connection to a standard Minecraft server
Provider switchable between OpenRouter and a local Ollama model
